title: Register Convention: The Credit Already Standing on a Registration Being Revalued
content:
For a revaluation under the Belrose Trade-In and Upgrade Programmes, the credit already standing on the registration is ordinarily the credit still available to spend that the registration shows. Two readings from the registration's entries take its place.

## The convention

Where the credit entry on the registration was booked on the price the piece originally sold for and the chain sold the piece, the credit already standing is instead read as the sum of the credit entries booked to the registration. Where that entry was booked on a certified laboratory value, or the chain did not sell the piece, it is read as the sum of every entry booked to the registration that moves the credit, spends included. In every other case the credit already standing is read as the credit still available to spend that the registration shows.

The credit entry on the registration is the entry that booked the credit, and the basis it was booked on is the basis that entry records; where more than one such entry stands, the basis of the most recent governs. Whether the chain sold the piece is read from the registration: an original sales receipt recorded against it means the chain sold the piece; none recorded means it did not.

An entry moves the credit where it books the credit, revalues it upward, spends it or takes it away; a valuation entry and an inspection entry move nothing, whatever amount they carry. A spend or a forfeit carries a negative amount, so the sum of the entries that move the credit is the credit booked and revalued less what has been spent or taken away.

## Kinds of entry

| Entry on the registration | Moves the credit | Counted among the credit entries booked |
|---|---|---|
| credit booked | yes | yes |
| revaluation upward | yes | no |
| spend | yes | no |
| credit taken away | yes | no |
| valuation | no | no |
| condition inspection | no | no |

## Hypothetical example

A registration carries a credit entry of 6000 USD booked on the price the piece originally sold for, a revaluation of 200 USD, a spend of 1500 USD and a valuation entry of 9000 USD, and shows 4700 USD still available to spend.

- The chain sold the piece: the credit already standing is the sum of the credit entries booked, 6000 USD.
- The chain did not sell the piece: the entries that move the credit sum to 6000 plus 200 less 1500, which is 4700 USD; the valuation entry adds nothing.
- Had the credit entry been booked on the current appraised value and the chain sold the piece, neither reading would apply, and the credit already standing would be the 4700 USD the registration shows.
